question: What is the main underlying issue in a patient with gastroparesis?

options.A: Severe inflammation and sores in the small bowel lining
options.B: Delayed stomach emptying even though there is no physical blockage
options.C: A total loss of the protective mucus barrier in the stomach
options.D: Food moving so fast it goes straight into the colon

explanation: In gastroparesis, the stomach is just too slow at emptying its contents. There's no tumor or physical blockage—it's usually a muscle or nerve issue!

question: Which of the following practices regarding alcohol is safest for a nursing mother?

options.A: Consuming alcohol immediately before every single nursing session to relax the baby
options.B: Mixing alcohol directly into infant formula to help the baby sleep through the night
options.C: Drinking large amounts of beer daily because it is traditionally believed to boost milk supply
options.D: Avoiding heavy or frequent drinking and waiting several hours after a drink before nursing

explanation: Alcohol enters breast milk quickly, so minimizing intake and allowing time for the body to clear it protects the infant. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h7)

question: Why does controlling rabies require teamwork between human health workers and vets?

options.A: The virus resides in animal reservoirs but causes fatal disease in humans
options.B: Veterinarians are trained to diagnose human psychiatric disorders
options.C: Animals can take human medications to cure their infections
options.D: Rabies is primarily spread through contaminated well water

explanation: Since dogs and wildlife are the main reservoir, we have to treat the animal population while also giving life-saving shots to exposed humans.

question: What is the recommended infant feeding practice for mothers living on ART where replacement feeding is unsafe?

options.A: Exclusive use of herbal teas and plain water
options.B: Immediate weaning onto cow milk on day one
options.C: Strict formula feeding without any breast milk
options.D: Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding combined with maternal ART provides the best balance of nutrition and protection against HIV transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: Which Nigerian law provides key legal protections against child abuse and exploitation?

options.A: The Federal Highway Traffic Code
options.B: The National Tax Administration Act
options.C: The Petroleum Industry Act
options.D: The Child Rights Act

explanation: Great job! The Child Rights Act is the foundational law that protects minors across Nigeria.

question: What is the simplest way to describe what a drug does in the body?

options.A: Any synthetic material used strictly for laboratory testing
options.B: A compound that creates entirely new cellular functions in organs
options.C: Any chemical substance that alters biological function in a living body
options.D: A natural substance derived exclusively from plants for nourishment

explanation: Spot on! Drugs work by modifying what your body is already doing—they don't magically invent brand-new functions. You've got this!

question: In a hospital, what do we mean by 'interdepartmental relationships'?

options.A: The personal friendships formed between nurses on the same shift
options.B: How different professional groups work together across hospital boundaries
options.C: The financial transactions between the hospital and medical suppliers
options.D: How doctors communicate exclusively with senior nursing staff

explanation: You've got this! Interdepartmental relationships simply mean teamwork and smooth communication between different units or departments in the hospital—like pharmacy working hand-in-hand with the ward.

question: How would you correctly name a small, fluid-filled blister from a mild burn?

options.A: Nodule
options.B: Scale
options.C: Macule
options.D: Vesicle

explanation: A vesicle is the clinical term for a small, fluid-filled skin bump or blister, often seen in early burns or chickenpox.

question: What is the main job of the skin when acting as a sense organ?

options.A: Filtering waste products from the bloodstream
options.B: Regulating the body's internal water balance
options.C: Relaying environmental information to the brain
options.D: Producing red blood cells for circulation

explanation: You've got this! The skin is packed with special nerve endings that pick up touch, temperature, and pain, sending those quick messages right up to your central nervous system.

question: What is the key sign of compartment syndrome that sets it apart from normal broken bone pain?

options.A: Mild aching pain that only occurs when the patient tries to walk
options.B: A gradual itching sensation underneath the plaster cast shell
options.C: Severe pain that is not relieved by standard opioid pain medications
options.D: Complete absence of any pain due to sudden nerve death

explanation: When pain is extreme and doesn't get better even with strong painkillers, think compartment syndrome! It means dangerous pressure is building up inside the muscle compartments.

question: Why do nurses routinely check a urine sample (urinalysis) when evaluating new urine leaks?

options.A: To check for a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine the patient's blood type
options.C: To screen for prostate cancer markers
options.D: To measure exact kidney filtration rates

explanation: Infections can irritate the bladder and cause sudden leaks. Ruling out an infection is always a smart first step in nursing assessment.

question: What classic physical change is often seen with long-term steroid therapy (cushingoid features)?

options.A: Yellowing skin
options.B: Excessive hair loss
options.C: Enlarged hands
options.D: Moon face

explanation: A round, puffy face—often called a 'moon face'—is a classic sign that the body has been exposed to extra corticosteroids over time.

question: Which of these is a common symptom of the genitourinary syndrome of menopause?

options.A: Excessive facial hair growth
options.B: Vaginal dryness and painful intercourse
options.C: Uncontrolled weight gain in the abdomen
options.D: Permanent loss of bladder sensation

explanation: Low estrogen makes the vaginal tissues thinner and drier, causing discomfort. Knowing this helps us care for patients with empathy.

question: Which muscle group acts like a supportive hammock at the bottom of the pelvis?

options.A: Rectus abdominis muscles
options.B: Detrusor muscle group
options.C: Levator ani muscle group
options.D: Abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Think of the levator ani as a strong sling or hammock holding all your pelvic organs neatly in place. Great job!

question: In a reflex arc, which part is responsible for catching the very first sign of trouble (like heat or pressure)?

options.A: Effector
options.B: Integration center
options.C: Motor neuron
options.D: Receptor

explanation: You got it! Receptors are like tiny guards in your skin and tissues waiting to pick up changes like heat, stretch, or pressure to kick off the reflex.

question: Why is food safety especially critical for patients with weakened immune systems?

options.A: Their bodies struggle to fight off foodborne infections
options.B: Bad water changes their skin color
options.C: Dirty food automatically stops medicines from working
options.D: Uncooked meat increases muscle mass too fast

explanation: Spot on! An immune system that is down cannot easily fight off germs from bad food, leading to serious illness.

question: About how long is the adult female urethra?

options.A: 12 centimeters
options.B: 4 centimeters
options.C: 20 centimeters
options.D: 30 centimeters

explanation: You've got this! The female urethra is quite short (about 4 cm), which makes catheterization quick, though it also means bacteria have a shorter trip to cause trouble.

question: Why might an elderly patient with slow kidneys need a smaller drug dose?

options.A: Cellular receptors disappear entirely from target tissues
options.B: Excretion is slower, increasing the risk of drug accumulation and toxicity
options.C: Absorption in the stomach increases rapidly with advanced age
options.D: Liver metabolism stops working completely after age sixty

explanation: When kidneys clear drugs more slowly, the medicine hangs around longer. Adjusting doses prevents accidental overload. Makes sense, right?

question: Why is eye care so important for a patient with Bell's palsy affecting Cranial Nerve VII?

options.A: The patient experiences excessive tearing that can blur vision permanently.
options.B: Infection in the inner ear spreads directly to the eyeball.
options.C: Increased pressure behind the eye causes the pupil to dilate permanently.
options.D: The inability to close the eyelid fully puts the cornea at risk of drying and ulceration.

explanation: Exactly right! Because Bell's palsy can stop the eye from closing all the way, we must protect the cornea from drying out.

question: What type of cartilage stays on the ends of bones inside your movable joints throughout life?

options.A: Elastic cartilage
options.B: Fibrocartilage pad
options.C: Epiphyseal cartilage
options.D: Articular cartilage

explanation: Articular cartilage acts like a smooth cushion on the ends of your bones so they can glide past each other smoothly in your joints.

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after sustaining a needle stick injury while on duty?

options.A: Hide the incident from the supervisor to avoid paperwork
options.B: Report the incident immediately for evaluation and prophylaxis
options.C: Soak the injured finger in cold river water
options.D: Take a strong painkiller and finish the remaining shift

explanation: Always report immediately! Quick action allows the occupational health team to give you prompt counseling and protective meds.

question: Why does Superior Vena Cava Syndrome cause facial swelling?

options.A: Allergic reactions to chemotherapy puff up the face
options.B: Lymph nodes in the neck shrink and pull skin tight
options.C: Blood flow from the head and neck is blocked from reaching the heart
options.D: Fluid retention is caused by failing kidneys

explanation: When a tumor blocks the superior vena cava, blood backs up in the upper body, causing noticeable swelling in the face, neck, and arms. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h3)

question: How should a nurse properly document physical examination findings?

options.A: Use vague words like 'fine' or 'normal' to save time
options.B: Let patients write their own clinical findings in the chart
options.C: Record findings objectively using clear measurements and descriptive terms
options.D: Wait until the end of the work week to write all notes at once

explanation: Clear, factual, and measured notes help the rest of the healthcare team truly understand how the patient is doing without guessing.

question: How does an autoclave primarily sterilize infectious waste?

options.A: By utilizing high-pressure, saturated steam to destroy pathogens
options.B: By exposing waste items to ultraviolet solar radiation for days
options.C: By burning organic materials into fine gray ash at very high heat
options.D: By dissolving plastic components in concentrated chemical solvents

explanation: Awesome! Autoclaves use pressurized steam to kill off stubborn germs effectively. You're mastering hospital equipment!

question: What color should the nurse tell the patient their stool might appear for a few days after a barium swallow?

options.A: Bright red or bloody
options.B: Jet black and tarry
options.C: Neon green or yellow
options.D: Chalky white or light gray

explanation: The elimination of residual unabsorbed barium sulfate naturally turns the stool a pale, chalky white or gray color until it is completely cleared. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h7)

question: What actually happens during the 'promotion' stage of cancer development?

options.A: Mutated cells are stimulated to divide over and over
options.B: Cancer cells immediately travel to the brain
options.C: All abnormal cells safely destroy themselves
options.D: Normal DNA is completely repaired by enzymes

explanation: During promotion, things like lifestyle factors or irritants encourage those already-changed cells to keep multiplying into a bigger problem.

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just do everything for a slow patient who can manage with a tool?

options.A: To save nursing time for charting and other patients
options.B: To ensure the patient finishes dressing before visiting hours
options.C: To foster independence and prevent learned helplessness
options.D: Because hospital policy strictly forbids nurse assistance

explanation: Brilliant! We want to cheer them on to do it themselves so they don't become overly dependent on us.

question: Why would a doctor order an antibody blood test for someone with a suspected endocrine problem?

options.A: To test how quickly the kidneys filter out waste products
options.B: To determine if the patient has a bacterial infection
options.C: To check for autoimmune destruction of endocrine tissue
options.D: To measure the exact weight and size of the pituitary gland

explanation: Spot on! Antibody tests help us see if the body's immune system is mistakenly attacking its own hormone glands, like in thyroid disorders.

question: Why is an oral dose of an opioid usually higher than its intravenous (IV) dose?

options.A: Intravenous injections bypass the bloodstream completely.
options.B: Intravenous drugs are absorbed much slower by body tissues.
options.C: The digestive tract destroys all active ingredients instantly.
options.D: Oral drugs undergo significant first-pass breakdown in the liver.

explanation: When you swallow a pill, it passes through the liver first and some of the drug gets metabolized. IV drugs skip this trip, so you need less of them!

question: Why does the body slow down digestion during pregnancy?

options.A: To allow more time for absorbing nutrients
options.B: To keep the maternal body temperature stable
options.C: To reduce pressure on the urinary bladder
options.D: To prevent the stomach from overstretching

explanation: Think of it as a helpful feature: slower digestion gives the body extra time to soak up all those important vitamins and nutrients for the growing baby!

question: Why is it so crucial that a patient stays completely still during a spine CT scan?

options.A: Sudden movement triggers an emergency shutdown of the X-ray tube
options.B: Patient motion alters the chemical makeup of the radioactive dye
options.C: Body movement creates motion artifact that blurs the images and impairs diagnosis
options.D: Moving too fast can damage the sensitive internal rotating glass detectors

explanation: Even a tiny wiggle can blur the images (we call this 'motion artifact'), making it hard for the doctor to spot a fracture or issue.

question: How is a short fallopian tube most commonly discovered in a clinical setting?

options.A: Through routine screening blood tests for hormone levels
options.B: Because of chronic lower back pain and fever
options.C: During infertility workups or incidental pelvic imaging
options.D: During routine breast examination and palpation

explanation: Short tubes usually don't cause pain on their own. They are usually spotted when doctors investigate why a patient is having trouble conceiving, or during scans done for other reasons.

question: Which of the following is NOT an ethical responsibility of the nurse regarding genetic test results?

options.A: Providing accurate and non-judgmental information
options.B: Respecting the autonomy of the patient in decision-making
options.C: Sharing the results openly with extended family members without consent
options.D: Maintaining strict patient confidentiality to prevent discrimination

explanation: Nurses must protect patient privacy and confidentiality; sharing genetic results without explicit consent violates ethical standards. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h6)

question: What does an autoclave primarily use to sterilize infectious medical waste?

options.A: High-pressure steam
options.B: Dry freezing air
options.C: Strong electric currents
options.D: Ultraviolet radiation

explanation: Autoclaves rely on pressurized steam to reach temperatures high enough to destroy bacteria, viruses, and spores. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h4)

question: What happens when a patient suffers damage specifically to Wernicke's area?

options.A: They lose voluntary movement in their right arm
options.B: They become completely blind in both eyes
options.C: They struggle to understand spoken and written language
options.D: They lose the ability to feel hot and cold temperatures

explanation: Wernicke's area is responsible for language comprehension rather than physical speech production. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h4)

question: What does 'pharmacokinetics' actually mean?

options.A: The financial cost of manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: The chemical structure of a synthetic compound
options.C: How a medication binds to specific cellular receptors
options.D: What the body does to a drug through absorption and excretion

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as the journey of the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. You can master this!

question: Which landmark document formally launched the modern health promotion movement in 1986?

options.A: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.B: The Abuja Declaration
options.C: The Nightingale Pledge
options.D: The Ottawa Charter

explanation: The Ottawa Charter of 1986 defined the core strategies for health promotion on a global scale. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: A patient asks if it's safe to use harsh medicated soaps to scrub away a rash. What should you tell them?

options.A: Mix the soap with bleach to ensure all potential germs are killed instantly
options.B: Use them twice a day to scrub away the scales faster than normal
options.C: Apply the soap directly to open wounds to speed up the drying process
options.D: Avoid harsh soaps and chemical bleaching creams because they can worsen skin inflammation

explanation: Well done! Harsh soaps strip away the skin's natural oils and can easily turn a mild rash into a painful flare-up.

question: A patient with completely clear breathing sounds inhaled a toxic gas two hours ago. What should you, as the nurse, expect to do?

options.A: Withholding all intravenous fluids to prevent lung fluid overload
options.B: Ordering a baseline chest X-ray and monitoring for delayed edema
options.C: Performing an immediate surgical tracheostomy in the ward
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately since lungs are currently clear

explanation: Don't let clear lungs fool you! Inhaled toxins can trigger dangerous fluid buildup (edema) in the lungs hours later, so keep a close eye on them.

question: What does inter-sectoral collaboration mean in the context of rehabilitation?

options.A: Working together across different fields like education, housing, and health
options.B: Requiring every patient to work in government offices
options.C: Merging all non-governmental groups into a single department
options.D: Leaving all recovery decisions strictly to hospital physicians

explanation: A patient's life involves more than just medicine. Bringing education, housing, and health sectors together ensures all of their needs are met.

question: Why is it important to check up on your patient after giving an injection or IV medication?

options.A: It ensures the medication achieved its intended effect and checks for adverse reactions.
options.B: It proves to the hospital pharmacy that the correct vial was opened.
options.C: It satisfies legal billing requirements for injectable supplies.
options.D: It replaces the need to check vital signs prior to administration.

explanation: You nailed it! Because injections work fast, following up helps you catch any early side effects and make sure the patient is feeling better.

question: What is the main job of the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: To filter waste products out of the kidneys
options.B: To transport blood between the heart and lungs
options.C: To absorb nutrients from digested food
options.D: To deliver oxygen directly to the brain

explanation: You got this! Pulmonary circulation simply moves blood between your heart and lungs so your red blood cells can drop off carbon dioxide and pick up fresh oxygen.

question: How does the water seal chamber stop air from rushing back into the patient's chest?

options.A: It uses electronic suction to block all backward movement of gases
options.B: It freezes the tubing shut whenever the patient tries to breathe in
options.C: It creates a chemical barrier that destroys outside bacteria instantly
options.D: It acts as a one-way valve that lets air out but not back in

explanation: Think of it like a one-way street! Air bubbles out when the patient breathes out, but the water blocks outside air from getting back in.

question: How do hospitals keep imaging going during sudden power outages?

options.A: Utilizing backup generators and battery-powered portable units
options.B: Performing manual sketches of internal organs at the bedside
options.C: Canceling all diagnostic imaging tests for the entire week
options.D: Waiting indefinitely until the public electricity grid restores power

explanation: Backup generators and portable machines are lifesavers when the main power grid goes down in clinical settings.

question: Which of these is a classic example of a dependent nursing intervention in the ICU?

options.A: Assessing a patient's pain level using a standard rating scale
options.B: Providing basic hygiene care and bed baths
options.C: Titrating a continuous vasopressor drip per doctor's protocol
options.D: Turning a ventilated patient every two hours to prevent sores

explanation: Dependent means it depends on a doctor's order! Powerful drugs like vasopressors need a physician's backup before you can adjust them.

question: How can intestinal tapeworms occasionally lead to a surgical emergency like appendicitis?

options.A: By causing massive allergic reactions throughout the abdominal cavity
options.B: By having worm segments physically block or lodge inside the appendiceal lumen
options.C: By migrating directly through the bloodstream into the liver tissue
options.D: By producing toxins that instantly rupture the intestinal wall

explanation: You nailed it! A wandering tapeworm segment can accidentally wedge itself inside the tiny appendix tube, causing a painful blockage and inflammation.

question: A nurse notices that people living near a stagnant river frequently catch malaria. What type of community is this?

options.A: Community of solution
options.B: Community of orientation
options.C: Virtual health community
options.D: Geographical community

explanation: Spot on! Because they share a specific physical location near that river, they share the same environmental health risks.

question: Why do we have a structured referral system between primary clinics and large teaching hospitals?

options.A: Preventing tertiary hospitals from ever seeing complex cases
options.B: Ensuring patients receive the appropriate level of care efficiently
options.C: Increasing the financial cost of routine patient visits
options.D: Keeping patients in primary clinics for as long as possible

explanation: Exactly! The referral system makes sure patients get sent to the right facility that has the exact equipment and specialists they need.

question: A patient is prescribed a new synergistic drug combo. What is a key nursing duty before giving it?

options.A: Restricting the patient from drinking any water for 24 hours
options.B: Telling the patient they can double the dose if pain increases
options.C: Checking baseline organ function tests and verify correct dosing
options.D: Stopping all other routine medications without physician approval

explanation: As a sharp nurse, you always check baseline labs like kidney and liver function first to make sure the patient can safely handle the combination.

question: Why do sutures need to be taken out instead of left inside the body permanently?

options.A: Skin cells will permanently grow over the thread and trap it in bone.
options.B: Non-absorbable threads act as foreign objects that can trigger infection.
options.C: The body will naturally dissolve all types of suture material within a week.
options.D: Permanent synthetic threads interfere with normal skin sensation forever.

explanation: Non-absorbable materials do not break down inside the body and will cause chronic irritation or abscess formation if left indefinitely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: What happens when an anticholinergic drug successfully binds to a receptor on the bladder?

options.A: The muscle contracts harder to empty the bladder completely
options.B: Normal muscle contractions are blocked, preventing spasms
options.C: Urine production in the kidneys stops temporarily
options.D: Blood flow to the urinary tract increases significantly

explanation: By occupying the spot, the drug blocks acetylcholine from turning on the squeeze switch, giving the bladder a chance to rest.

question: Which of these is a physical safety feature (engineering control) built to stop sharps injuries?

options.A: Retractable scalpel blades
options.B: Doing yearly staff performance reviews
options.C: Giving verbal warnings across the theatre table
options.D: Wearing plain cotton scrub suits

explanation: Engineering controls are physical tools or devices built right into equipment—like a retractable blade—to keep us safe from accidental cuts.

question: Why must a community health nurse be versatile and take on multiple roles like educator, manager, and clinician?

options.A: To ensure that administrative paperwork takes up the entire workday
options.B: To effectively address the wide variety of health and social needs in a population
options.C: To avoid working with community leaders and traditional health practitioners
options.D: To replace local doctors in diagnosing and performing major surgeries

explanation: Because community settings present complex social and health problems, nurses must switch between teaching, managing, and direct care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h2)

question: Which nursing theory focuses heavily on helping a person or community practice self-care?

options.A: Florence Nightingale's Environmental Theory
options.B: Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Sigmund Freud's Psychosexual Theory
options.D: Abraham Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs

explanation: Spot on! Orem's model is all about empowering people with the skills they need to take charge of their own health.

question: In a life-threatening poisoning emergency, which route of administration is generally preferred for antidotes?

options.A: Intravenous
options.B: Transdermal
options.C: Subcutaneous
options.D: Rectal suppository

explanation: The IV route puts the antidote straight into the bloodstream so it can start working almost immediately when every second counts.

question: Which event officially marks day one of the menstrual cycle?

options.A: The cessation of progesterone production
options.B: The release of a mature egg
options.C: The thickening of the uterine wall
options.D: The start of menstrual bleeding

explanation: You've got this! Day one of the cycle always starts on the very first day that bleeding begins. Think of it as the official reset button for the cycle.

question: Why do nurses need to be extra careful when giving sleeping pills to older adult patients?

options.A: Older adults process drugs faster, rendering the pills useless
options.B: Sleeping pills increase the risk of daytime drowsiness and accidental falls
options.C: Older adults are legally barred from taking sleeping medications
options.D: Sedatives always cause severe allergic reactions in senior patients

explanation: Sedatives can linger in an older adult's system, causing grogginess and unsteady legs during the day. This puts them at high risk for falls!

question: How can strict, old-fashioned gender roles negatively affect relationships?

options.A: They encourage equal sharing of household responsibilities
options.B: They can promote power imbalances and discourage emotional expression
options.C: They ensure that partners always agree on financial decisions
options.D: They eliminate all forms of misunderstandings between couples

explanation: Exactly! When society forces rigid boxes on how men and women must behave, it often stops open communication and creates unfair power dynamics.

question: What is another common medical term for a joint?

options.A: Articulation
options.B: Cartilage plate
options.C: Ligament
options.D: Tendinous band

explanation: Spot on! In anatomy and nursing, we call a joint an articulation because it's the exact point where two or more bones meet.

question: What is a major challenge that often stops clients from completing a family planning referral?

options.A: High transportation costs and distance to the receiving facility
options.B: Excessive availability of feedback slips in the primary clinic
options.C: Having too many free contraceptive options available at home
options.D: Too much emotional support provided by community health nurses

explanation: Long distances and transport money wahala are real hurdles that can discourage clients from making the trip to a secondary center.

question: What is the best way to write down a skin problem in a patient's nursing chart?

options.A: Write the single word 'rash' to save precious time
options.B: Provide precise dimensions, color, and anatomical location
options.C: Guess the exact disease name without checking physical signs
options.D: Record only what the family members report about the spots

explanation: Be specific! Writing down exact measurements, colors, and where it is on the body helps the whole healthcare team track changes accurately.

question: What is the main job of the foramen ovale in a baby before birth?

options.A: Connect the pulmonary artery directly to the aorta
options.B: Drain waste products directly into the umbilical vein
options.C: Supply oxygenated blood to the developing liver tissue
options.D: Shunt blood from the right atrium to the left atrium

explanation: Great job! Before birth, a baby's lungs aren't being used yet. The foramen ovale acts like a shortcut door between the upper heart chambers, letting oxygen-rich blood skip the resting lungs and head straight out to the body.

question: Which form of a drug molecule passes most easily across biological cell membranes?

options.A: Ionized
options.B: Conjugated
options.C: Unionized
options.D: Protein-bound

explanation: Unionized (un-charged) drug molecules are more fat-friendly (lipophilic), helping them slip smoothly across cell membranes.

question: A patient with an external fixator on their leg says a metal pin site feels a bit tender. What should you do first?

options.A: Inspect the pin site for signs of infection, redness, or purulent drainage.
options.B: Remove the metal pin immediately to relieve the local pressure.
options.C: Document the finding as normal and schedule a follow-up in six months.
options.D: Apply a tight elastic bandage directly over the protruding pins.

explanation: Since pins go through the skin, they can easily invite bacteria in. Checking the site closely helps you catch early signs of infection or osteomyelitis. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: What is the medical term for difficulty swallowing experienced by many clients with degenerative disorders?

options.A: Dysuria
options.B: Dysphagia
options.C: Dyspnea
options.D: Dyspepsia

explanation: Dysphagia refers to impaired swallowing mechanics caused by muscle weakness or neurological damage. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h6)

question: How do chronic stressors differ from acute stressors?

options.A: Chronic stressors only affect psychological well-being
options.B: Acute stressors last for months or years
options.C: Chronic stressors persist over a long period without relief
options.D: Acute stressors cause no physiological response

explanation: Think of acute stress as a sudden flash flood (short and intense), while chronic stress is like a long-term drought that wears you down over months or years.

question: What is the primary function of the autonomic nervous system?

options.A: Storing long-term memories in the brain
options.B: Regulating involuntary body functions
options.C: Controlling voluntary skeletal muscles
options.D: Processing conscious thoughts and logic

explanation: The autonomic nervous system works automatically to control internal organs and involuntary processes without conscious effort. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h1)

question: Why should anti-diarrhoea drugs that slow down the gut be avoided in certain bacterial infections?

options.A: They immediately destroy all beneficial gut bacteria
options.B: They permanently stop the kidneys from producing urine
options.C: They cause severe spikes in systemic blood pressure
options.D: Trapping toxins inside the bowel can worsen the illness

explanation: If a patient has a nasty bacterial infection, their body needs to flush the germs out. Slowing down the gut traps those bad toxins inside, which can make them much sicker.

question: A new mother bleeds heavily because a small piece of the placenta was left behind in the uterus. Which of the 4 Ts does this fall under?

options.A: Thrombin
options.B: Tone
options.C: Trauma
options.D: Tissue

explanation: When membranes or pieces of the placenta stay behind inside, we group that under 'Tissue'. Making sure the placenta is complete upon delivery prevents this!

question: Why do many nurses feel more emotional weight when turning off a ventilator compared to deciding not to start one?

options.A: Because stopping an active machine feels like a direct action causing death
options.B: Because hospital policies strictly forbid withdrawing mechanical ventilation
options.C: Because family members are never allowed to witness ventilator removal
options.D: Because withholding treatment requires more paperwork than withdrawing

explanation: Physically reaching out to switch off life support feels heavy emotionally, even though ethically and legally, letting nature take its course is the same in both cases.

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?

options.A: Investigation, Environment, and Community
options.B: Immunization, Education, and Care
options.C: Information, Education, and Communication
options.D: Infection, Evaluation, and Control

explanation: IEC is a core public health strategy that stands for Information, Education, and Communication, used to guide community health promotion. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why is it best to count a patient's breathing rate discreetly without telling them right away?

options.A: It saves time during a busy hospital shift to count during pulse checks
options.B: Patients will feel anxious if they know their lungs are being watched
options.C: Unconscious patients are the only ones who have true resting rates
options.D: Conscious awareness can alter the patient's normal breathing rate and depth

explanation: When people know you are watching them breathe, they naturally start controlling it. Counting while pretending to check the pulse is a smart clinical trick! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is the major black-box warning linked to the long-term use of propylthiouracil (PTU)?

options.A: Severe liver injury and acute liver failure
options.B: Sudden permanent blindness from optic neuritis
options.C: Massive kidney stone formation and renal colic
options.D: Rapid deterioration of bone density and fractures

explanation: PTU carries a serious warning about liver damage, which is why nurses always keep an eye out for liver function test results.

question: Why must a chest drainage system always stay lower than the patient's chest level?

options.A: To ensure the suction motor runs quietly without disturbing the patient
options.B: To use gravity effectively and prevent fluid from flowing backward into the pleural space
options.C: To make it easier for the patient to ambulate around the room
options.D: To prevent the water-seal chamber from evaporating too quickly

explanation: Gravity is our best friend here; keeping the collection box down ensures fluid drains away from the patient, not back into them. You've got a bright future in ward nursing!

question: Which of these is part of the body's first line of defence?

options.A: Circulating blood antibodies
options.B: Intact skin and mucous membranes
options.C: Phagocytic white blood cells
options.D: Specialized T-lymphocyte cells

explanation: You got it! Your skin and mucous membranes act like a brick wall at the gate, stopping germs from entering your body in the first place.

question: What is the main job of the vital centres in your body?

options.A: Processing conscious thoughts and logic
options.B: Storing long-term memories and emotions
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movements
options.D: Managing basic life-sustaining functions automatically

explanation: You don't have to think about breathing or your heart beating! Vital centres run these automatic survival tasks behind the scenes.

question: Where does fertilization usually happen inside the fallopian tube?

options.A: Infundibulum
options.B: Isthmus
options.C: Ampulla
options.D: Fimbriae

explanation: Brilliant! The ampulla is the wide middle part of the tube where the sperm and egg love to meet.

question: Years after getting a vaccine, why can your body fight off the same infection so much faster?

options.A: White blood cells permanently increase their normal physical size
options.B: The original vaccine stays active inside the bloodstream forever
options.C: Circulating antibiotics permanently block all future viruses
options.D: Immunological memory allows a rapid secondary response

explanation: You've got this! Your immune system has a great memory. It remembers past encounters and mounts a quick, powerful defense when the real germ shows up later.

question: Why do nurses do a baseline neurologic assessment when a patient is first admitted?

options.A: To determine the exact cost of hospital care
options.B: To replace the need for diagnostic imaging scans
options.C: To cure underlying nerve cell damage
options.D: To detect any changes in patient status over time

explanation: Think of a baseline as your starting snapshot! It gives you a reference point so if the patient's condition changes later, you can spot it right away.

question: Which communication habit helps build healthy, positive relationships?

options.A: Keeping all emotions hidden to avoid conflict
options.B: Interrupting the speaker to show dominance
options.C: Using 'I' statements to express personal feelings
options.D: Blaming the partner for every disagreement

explanation: Spot on! Saying 'I feel...' instead of 'You always...' stops the other person from getting defensive and opens the door to honest conversation.

question: Why is closely monitoring urine output so crucial for a patient with sepsis?

options.A: It proves that the patient is drinking enough oral fluids
options.B: It is a reliable indicator of adequate kidney perfusion and fluid status
options.C: It prevents the bladder from becoming distended during sleep
options.D: It eliminates the need to check blood pressure every hour

explanation: Urine output is our window into how well the kidneys and vital organs are getting blood flow. Good urine output means the body is holding up against shock!

question: How does progestin mainly prevent sperm from reaching an egg?

options.A: By destroying sperm in the vagina
options.B: By increasing the temperature of the uterus
options.C: By blocking the fallopian tubes physically
options.D: By thickening the cervical mucus

explanation: You've got this! Progestin changes the thickness of cervical fluid, creating a strong barrier that makes it very hard for sperm to swim upward.

question: You are caring for a stroke patient. Which of these signs needs your immediate action to stop a life-threatening problem?

options.A: Coughing and wet-sounding voice while drinking water
options.B: A minor loss of memory regarding recent visitors
options.C: Slight weakness in the right upper and lower extremities
options.D: Mild frustration when attempting to button a shirt

explanation: Coughing or a gurgly voice right after drinking is a huge red flag for swallowing trouble (dysphagia). It means water might be going down the wrong pipe into the lungs, risking aspiration pneumonia!

question: What is the recommended method for handling a needle if a safety device is unavailable?

options.A: Ask a nearby colleague to hold the cap in place
options.B: Leave the needle uncapped on the procedure tray
options.C: Use a one-hand scoop technique to guide the cap on
options.D: Hold the cap firmly with both hands while sliding the needle

explanation: The one-handed scoop method prevents the fingers of the non-dominant hand from being accidentally poked. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is one major danger of poor communication between hospital departments?

options.A: Increased risk of sentinel events and medical errors
options.B: Faster patient discharge times across all units
options.C: Higher patient satisfaction ratings from families
options.D: Decreased workload for the nursing staff

explanation: That's right! When communication breaks down, critical information gets lost, which puts patient safety at serious risk.

question: A patient's surgical drain has accidentally fallen out onto the bed sheets. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Rinse the fallen tube with tap water and tape it to the skin
options.B: Cover the insertion site immediately with a sterile dressing
options.C: Leave the open hole uncovered to let the remaining fluid drain out
options.D: Put sterile gloves on and push the tube right back into the wound

explanation: Placing a sterile dressing over the hole protects the exposed tissue from bacteria, and you should never reinsert a fallen drain because it is no longer sterile. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is the main job of a regular surgical mask?

options.A: To supply extra oxygen
options.B: To filter out tiny microscopic viruses completely
options.C: To block large splashes, sprays, and droplets
options.D: To provide a tight, air-sealed fit around the face

explanation: Surgical masks are great shields against everyday hospital splashes and sprays, even though they don't seal tightly around your face.

question: Why must nurses check a patient's liver function before starting a long course of albendazole?

options.A: Healthy liver function prevents worms from entering the bloodstream
options.B: Liver cells store the medication for up to six months
options.C: Hepatic enzymes are needed to activate the drug in the stomach
options.D: The medication is metabolized primarily through the liver

explanation: Brilliant! Because the liver breaks down these drugs, we need to make sure it's healthy enough to handle the workload without causing toxicity.

question: Which professional is best suited to organize tricky medications into weekly blister packs for a patient?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Laboratory scientist
options.C: Hospital accountant
options.D: Pharmacist

explanation: Pharmacists are medication pros! They love helping patients sort out tricky schedules using pill organizers and blister packs.

question: Which of the following is a common management challenge in day care centres?

options.A: Complete absence of any government regulations
options.B: Too much space for very few enrolled children
options.C: High staff turnover and inadequate funding
options.D: Excessive numbers of trained medical doctors on site

explanation: Many day care centres struggle with financial constraints and frequent changes in caregiving staff, which can disrupt service quality. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h7)

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with 10 episodes of watery diarrhea today. Which assessment finding requires immediate nursing action?

options.A: Mild fussiness when the mother tries to feed him
options.B: Sunken fontanelle and no wet diapers for six hours
options.C: Mild low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Loose stool containing small pieces of undigested food

explanation: A sunken fontanelle and lack of wet diapers indicate dangerous dehydration and reduced kidney perfusion, requiring urgent fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: Which of these is the most common type of cancerous vulval tumour?

options.A: Basal cell skin carcinoma
options.B: Primary vulval melanoma
options.C: Squamous cell carcinoma
options.D: Bartholin gland adenocarcinoma

explanation: Correct! Squamous cell carcinoma makes up the vast majority of malignant vulval growths you will see in practice.

question: What term describes shaky, clumsy, and uncoordinated muscle movements caused by a problem in the cerebellum?

options.A: Akinetopsia
options.B: Apraxia
options.C: Aphasia
options.D: Ataxia

explanation: Ataxia is the loss of smooth muscle coordination. If the cerebellum (our balance center) is affected, movements can look clumsy and unsteady.

question: Why is double-checking the patient's ID band considered the absolute most important rule before a blood transfusion?

options.A: It ensures the hospital billing department charges the correct patient
options.B: It guarantees the blood donor receives proper compensation
options.C: It prevents clerical errors that can cause fatal incompatible reactions
options.D: It speeds up the time it takes to deliver blood from the lab

explanation: Spotting identity mistakes saves lives! Giving blood to the wrong person is a major cause of dangerous reactions, making this check vital.

question: What are you trying to find out when you perform Leopold's maneuvers on a pregnant client?

options.A: To check the mother's cardiovascular health status
options.B: To stimulate the uterus into early contraction
options.C: To determine fetal lie, presentation, and engagement
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the placenta

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just feeling the bump with your hands to figure out how the baby is curled up and positioned inside as delivery gets closer.

question: Which structure is the main maker of progesterone during the second half of the menstrual cycle?

options.A: Corpus luteum
options.B: Anterior pituitary
options.C: Adrenal cortex
options.D: Graafian follicle

explanation: After ovulation, the empty follicle transforms into the corpus luteum, which acts like a little hormone factory pumping out progesterone.

question: Why can untreated vaginal infections sometimes lead to fertility problems?

options.A: Infections can ascend into the upper reproductive tract and cause scarring.
options.B: Vaginal pH permanently drops to zero, destroying all gametes.
options.C: Inflammation triggers the immediate closure of the vaginal canal.
options.D: Pathogens consume all systemic estrogen needed for ovulation.

explanation: You nailed it! If ignored, germs can travel upward into the uterus and fallopian tubes, causing inflammation and scar tissue that can make getting pregnant harder later.

question: What do we call skin changes that show up directly as the very first sign of a disease process?

options.A: Vascular lesions
options.B: Primary lesions
options.C: Purpuric lesions
options.D: Secondary lesions

explanation: Spotting primary lesions helps you catch skin conditions right at the beginning before they change. You've got this!

question: What does the 'Proximity Principle' mean when dealing with hazardous waste?

options.A: It should be shipped overseas to countries with large open spaces
options.B: It must be stored as far away from human populations as possible
options.C: It must be kept in temporary storage for at least ten years
options.D: It should be disposed of as close to its source as possible

explanation: You got it! Keeping travel distances short means fewer chances for accidental spills or exposure while moving dangerous materials around.

question: What do we call the body's natural ability to keep its internal environment balanced and stable?

options.A: Homeostasis
options.B: Catabolism
options.C: Anabolism
options.D: Metabolism

explanation: Homeostasis is like the body's internal thermostat—it constantly works behind the scenes to keep everything stable, no matter what is happening around you! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h1)

question: When is it strictly necessary for a nurse to use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Only when starting a surgical procedure in the theater
options.B: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids
options.C: Whenever the alcohol dispenser is empty for the day
options.D: Every time a nurse enters a new hospital ward

explanation: Alcohol rubs cannot remove physical dirt or certain tough bacterial spores as effectively as physical washing with soap and water. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary tool midwives use to track the progress of labour on a chart?

options.A: Partograph
options.B: Growth curve
options.C: Bishoff scale
options.D: Apgar chart

explanation: The partograph gives us a neat visual story of how labour is going. It's our best friend for spotting slow progress or fetal distress early!

question: Why do doctors evaluate fertility after just six months for women aged thirty-five and older?

options.A: The uterine lining becomes too thick for implantation over time
options.B: Ovarian reserve and egg quality naturally decrease faster at this age
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives take longer to leave the body after age thirty-five
options.D: Older women have a higher rate of chronic pelvic infections

explanation: A quicker evaluation is helpful because a woman's egg quality and supply naturally start to decline faster in her late thirties. Keep up the good work!

question: Why are older adults with degenerative conditions at a higher risk for drug toxicity?

options.A: Their digestive tracts destroy all medications before absorption
options.B: They always take their pills at the wrong time of day
options.C: Their brains actively attract and store extra chemical compounds
options.D: Their liver and kidney functions naturally slow down with age

explanation: You got it! Because the liver and kidneys clear drugs from the body, when they age and slow down, medications can build up and lead to accidental toxicity. Always start low and go slow with older adults!

question: You want to start an immunization campaign in a rural town. What should be your very first step?

options.A: Consult with local leaders and respect community values
options.B: Import expensive foreign medications without checking needs
options.C: Call the police to force every parent to bring their child
options.D: Build a brand-new private hospital without telling residents

explanation: Spot on! Working hand-in-hand with local leaders builds immediate trust and ensures the community happily joins in to protect their health.

question: How are food nutrients mainly grouped based on how much the body needs them?

options.A: Macronutrients and micronutrients
options.B: Simple sugars and complex structures
options.C: Soluble and insoluble compounds
options.D: Animal-based and plant-based elements

explanation: We group them by quantity! 'Macro' means large (like carbs and proteins we need in bulk), and 'micro' means small (like vitamins needed in tiny amounts). Easy peasy!

question: What is the most critical thing a nurse should teach a patient being discharged with chronic primary adrenal insufficiency?

options.A: How and when to administer emergency injectable hydrocortisone during acute stress or illness
options.B: Why strenuous physical exercise must be completely avoided for the rest of the patient's life
options.C: How to restrict daily dietary salt intake to prevent sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.D: Why it is safe to stop taking daily oral steroids once physical strength and appetite return

explanation: Teaching a patient how to use an emergency injection can literally save their life if a sudden crisis hits when they are far from a hospital.

question: Why is capillary bleeding usually less dangerous than arterial bleeding?

options.A: Capillary blood carries no oxygen
options.B: Capillaries carry blood under very low pressure, causing a slow ooze
options.C: Capillaries only exist in the dead outer skin layer
options.D: The body instantly clots capillaries without platelets

explanation: Because tiny capillaries have very low pressure, any bleeding from them usually trickles slowly rather than gushing out fast.

question: Why is it smart to check a menu for a nice mix of colors, textures, and flavors?

options.A: It guarantees that the food will require zero cooking preparation time
options.B: It stimulates appetite and makes the meal more enjoyable to eat
options.C: It prevents the kitchen staff from having to wash dishes afterwards
options.D: It ensures that every food item tastes exactly the same

explanation: Nobody wants a boring, pale plate! Colorful, well-textured food makes patients actually want to eat.

question: How does pharmacological action differ from therapeutic use?

options.A: It explains how the drug works in the body rather than what disease it treats
options.B: It tells the nurse how many pills the patient should swallow
options.C: It describes the financial cost of producing the medication
options.D: It is only used by pharmacists and never looked at by nurses

explanation: Pharmacological action focuses on the cellular or body mechanism, while therapeutic use focuses on the target illness. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h2)

question: A patient with lung cancer is still getting chemotherapy while also receiving care for severe pain and shortness of breath. What kind of approach is this?

options.A: Integrating palliative care alongside curative treatment
options.B: Treating the side effects of chemotherapy exclusively with surgery
options.C: Abandoning curative treatment in favor of hospice
options.D: Stopping all medical interventions to allow natural death

explanation: Brilliant! Patients don't have to choose just one. They can receive treatments to fight the illness (like chemotherapy) while simultaneously getting comfort care to manage their symptoms.

question: Why is having a nurse stay close and encourage a mother during active labor so helpful?

options.A: it directly accelerates cervical effacement by stimulating oxytocin receptors
options.B: it completely eliminates the biological need for pharmacological anesthesia
options.C: it helps reduce maternal anxiety and decreases the perceived intensity of pain
options.D: it prevents the occurrence of variable decelerations in the fetal heart rate

explanation: Well done! Continuous presence and a warm, reassuring voice lower stress and help mothers cope much better with contractions.

question: What is the primary cause of joint contractures in a person with severe physical immobility?

options.A: Sudden increases in blood pressure during physical exertion
options.B: Bacterial infections traveling from the bladder into the joint space
options.C: Permanent shortening of muscles and tendons from lack of movement
options.D: Excessive intake of dietary calcium forming deposits in the joints

explanation: When joints remain in one position without movement, the surrounding soft tissues shorten and stiffen, resulting in a contracture. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h4)

question: What do we mean by body alignment in nursing care?

options.A: How skeletal and muscular systems maintain balance against gravity
options.B: The physical distance a patient can walk without resting
options.C: A measurement of total muscle mass in the lower limbs
options.D: The specific angle at which a hospital bed is elevated

explanation: Think of body alignment as how your bones and muscles work together like a team to keep you upright and balanced against gravity, preventing strain.

question: Which behavior strongly suggests that a patient is dealing with high emotional stress?

options.A: Slow, deep, and regular breathing
options.B: Withdrawal and tearfulness
options.C: Eager participation in daily planning
options.D: Relaxed facial muscles and posture

explanation: When people feel overwhelmed emotionally, they often shut down, pull away from others, or break down in tears. Keep an eye out for these cues as a nurse! [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h5)

question: Why can relying solely on normal vital signs be misleading in a critically ill patient?

options.A: The body's compensatory mechanisms can hide internal decline for a while.
options.B: Normal ranges apply only to children, not adults.
options.C: Vital signs change every single second without reason.
options.D: Monitors are frequently broken in hospital environments.

explanation: Patients can push their heart rate and blood vessels to work harder to maintain normal numbers right up until their system suddenly crashes. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why must nurses specifically ask patients about over-the-counter painkillers during a medication review?

options.A: Patients often do not consider non-prescription drugs as 'real' medications to report
options.B: Non-prescription drugs completely cure all forms of arthritis
options.C: Over-the-counter drugs have no side effects on bones or joints
options.D: Patients are legally prohibited from taking pain relievers at home

explanation: Spot-on! Patients often forget to mention everyday painkillers they buy over the counter, even though they can cause side effects or interact with other drugs.

question: How do Class III antiarrhythmic drugs primarily affect the cardiac action potential?

options.A: They stop all electrical signals from leaving the ventricles
options.B: They speed up the initial sodium influx to hasten contraction
options.C: They delay repolarization to lengthen the refractory period
options.D: They open calcium gates wide to increase pumping strength

explanation: By blocking potassium channels, these drugs keep the cell in a resting, refractory state longer, preventing chaotic signals. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why does having a family history of menstrual pain increase a young person's chance of having dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Genetic factors influence prostaglandin production and pain sensitivity
options.B: Pain is a learned behavior that is copied from older relatives
options.C: Mothers intentionally pass uterine infections down to their daughters
options.D: Family members usually share identical dietary habits every day

explanation: You got it! Genetics play a big role in how our bodies handle inflammatory chemicals and how sensitive we are to pain.

question: Which hormone does the hypothalamus release in pulses to wake up the pituitary gland?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Luteinizing Hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone
options.D: Follicle-Stimulating Hormone

explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the master controller. It sends out Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) as a messenger signal to get the pituitary gland to join the action!

question: What is the main difference between being a manager and being a leader?

options.A: Managing hospital financial records
options.B: Inspiring people and driving positive change
options.C: Enforcing institutional policies strictly
options.D: Maintaining systems and controlling budgets

explanation: Management is about keeping the systems running and budgets balanced, but true leadership is all about motivating your team and guiding everyone toward a shared vision.

question: Why is home health care such an exciting shift in modern nursing?

options.A: It moves professional care from large hospitals back into the community
options.B: It focuses only on domestic chores rather than medical tasks
options.C: It completely replaces the need for doctors and clinics
options.D: It removes all responsibilities from family caregivers

explanation: Spot on! Instead of keeping everyone stuck in hospital wards, home care brings the healing right into the patient's familiar home environment.

question: Which situation is a classic slip, trip, and fall hazard?

options.A: A lab tech breathing in chemical vapor
options.B: An office worker stressed over deadlines
options.C: Water spilled across a busy hospital corridor
options.D: A welder exposed to UV light without a shield

explanation: Slippery walking surfaces directly increase the risk of falls, making them one of the most common physical safety hazards in any facility.

question: Why is physical therapy so important after breast cancer surgery?

options.A: To stimulate rapid hair growth after finishing chemotherapy sessions
options.B: To close surgical skin incisions faster without needing sutures
options.C: To reduce the patient's daily requirement for oral pain medication
options.D: To prevent shoulder stiffness and restore full movement of the arm

explanation: Chest and armpit surgery can make the shoulder freeze up. Gentle physiotherapy helps patients get their arm movement back completely.

question: Which physical sign is a reliable indicator that vital organs are getting enough blood flow?

options.A: Dry and cracked lips
options.B: Adequate urine output
options.C: Slow and deep breathing
options.D: Cold and pale fingers

explanation: Spot on, future nurse! Good urine output tells you the kidneys are well-perfused, meaning the heart and blood vessels are keeping good pressure up.

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective family planning referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: Short waiting times at all tertiary teaching hospitals
options.B: Financial constraints and inability to afford transport costs
options.C: Immediate feedback letters arriving within five minutes
options.D: Excessive availability of free transport services for all clients

explanation: Poverty and transport costs prevent many clients from reaching distant secondary or tertiary referral centers. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h7)

question: What was the main source of medicines used by ancient civilizations?

options.A: Genetically modified crops
options.B: Synthesized laboratory chemicals
options.C: Purified animal hormones
options.D: Plants and minerals found in nature

explanation: Before modern laboratories, early healers relied entirely on natural sources like roots, barks, leaves, and minerals to treat illnesses. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses need to understand both the law and professional ethics?

options.A: To bypass the need for patient consent during emergencies
options.B: To avoid breaking the law while giving kind, respectful care
options.C: To ensure hospitals never face financial audits
options.D: To successfully prosecute patients who break hospital rules

explanation: Knowing both legal rules and ethical principles protects you from trouble while making sure your patients always feel respected and cared for! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: Where do school health programs mainly take place?

options.A: Local community primary health centers
options.B: Educational institutions and classrooms
options.C: State-managed regional hospitals
options.D: Private pediatric specialty clinics

explanation: You got it! School health programs focus on schools because that's where children spend most of their day learning and growing.

question: What is the main purpose of regular team conferences in home health care?

options.A: To review patient progress and update the unified care plan
options.B: To reduce the number of home visits required by the agency
options.C: To replace written medical documentation in patient charts
options.D: To evaluate the personal performance of the nursing staff

explanation: Team conferences bring professionals together to share updates, evaluate goals, and adjust care strategies based on current needs. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h6)

question: In a neurovascular check for a injured limb, what does the letter 'P' stand for?

options.A: Pulselessness
options.B: Pressure
options.C: Perforation
options.D: Pruritus

explanation: Think of the 5 Ps: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, and Paralysis. They help us quickly spot nerve and blood flow issues!

question: Why do pharmacy teams do regular physical stock counts in a DRF?

options.A: To prove to patients that the building has air conditioning
options.B: To determine which medical doctor writes the most prescriptions
options.C: To ensure the pharmaceutical companies pay their annual taxes
options.D: To catch discrepancies between actual drug counts and record books

explanation: Great thinking! Counting physical items helps you spot missing stock, theft, or counting errors that paperwork won't show.

question: Why must a community health nurse look beyond just one patient at a time?

options.A: Because hospital policies require nurses to ignore personal health
options.B: Because collective environments and cultures directly influence health
options.C: Because public health laws forbid treating people one at a time
options.D: Because individual illnesses have no connection to living conditions

explanation: A person's health is heavily shaped by their surroundings and lifestyle. Looking at the big picture helps us care better!

question: What is the primary focus of a strategic plan in nursing management?

options.A: Immediate treatment of a single patient
options.B: Broad, long-term organizational goals
options.C: Ordering supplies for the current week
options.D: Daily shift scheduling and staff breaks

explanation: Strategic plans look years ahead and focus on the big-picture mission and direction of the entire healthcare facility. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take after experiencing a needle-stick injury?

options.A: Fill out an official hospital incident report form
options.B: Wash the affected skin thoroughly with soap and running water
options.C: Squeeze the wound tightly to force out as much blood as possible
options.D: Wait until the end of the shift to see if swelling develops

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral load introduced by the sharp object before it establishes infection. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is the main goal of Youth Friendly Services (YFS)?

options.A: To provide free medical treatment only for children
options.B: To attract and address the health needs of adolescents
options.C: To make hospitals run faster and more efficiently
options.D: To replace adult medical care entirely

explanation: You got it! YFS is all about creating a safe space tailored to the unique physical and emotional needs of young people.

question: Why is general supportive care often more critical than finding an antidote right away when someone is poisoned?

options.A: Supportive care keeps vital organs working while the body clears the toxin
options.B: Most poisons have strong antidotes available immediately
options.C: Antidotes only work if given within two minutes of exposure
options.D: Antidotes are too expensive to keep in most rural hospitals

explanation: Great thinking! Since we don't have a magical antidote for every single poison out there, keeping the patient's breathing and heart going buys enough time for their body to naturally process and clear the toxin.

question: Why do many Nigerian families prefer home health care for their sick relatives?

options.A: To completely avoid paying any hospital bills
options.B: To comply with mandatory national health insurance rules
options.C: To access advanced surgical theaters at home
options.D: To bypass long hospital queues and get personal attention

explanation: Spot on! Families love home care because it helps them dodge long hospital waits and gives their loved one undivided attention.

question: Why are babies born to unvaccinated mothers at such high risk for tetanus?

options.A: They are more susceptible to common household bacteria
options.B: They lack protective antibodies passed from the mother
options.C: Their umbilical cords take much longer to heal naturally
options.D: They fail to absorb nutrients from breast milk properly

explanation: You got it! When a mother is vaccinated during pregnancy, she passes protective antibodies to her baby to shield them until they can make their own.

question: What is one of the biggest dangers of leaving a patient in a wet or soiled adult diaper for too long?

options.A: Permanent kidney failure
options.B: Skin breakdown and pressure injury
options.C: Chronic high blood pressure
options.D: Sudden loss of upper body strength

explanation: Moisture and waste trap heat and wetness against the skin, breaking down its defenses fast. Keeping patients clean and dry is one of your core superpowers as a nurse!

question: What is the main goal of food and nutrition when caring for a patient receiving palliative care?

options.A: Reversing the underlying terminal disease
options.B: Building muscle mass and healing wounds
options.C: Extending life by forcing high calorie intake
options.D: Promoting comfort and quality of life

explanation: Great job thinking about holistic care! In palliative care, we focus on what brings the patient peace and enjoyment rather than trying to reverse the disease or force weight gain.

question: What does maternal morbidity primarily measure?

options.A: Illnesses and health problems resulting from pregnancy
options.B: Percentage of babies born with congenital abnormalities
options.C: Total number of women who die during childbirth
options.D: Rate of spontaneous miscarriages in the first trimester

explanation: Morbidity focuses on the illnesses, injuries, and health complications women survive during or after pregnancy, rather than death itself. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T015#GNS226_U1_T015_h1)

question: What is the main structural difference between a septate uterus and a bicornuate uterus?

options.A: A septate uterus has two distinct cervices, while a bicornuate uterus only has one.
options.B: A septate uterus has a normal outer shape with an internal wall, while a bicornuate uterus has a heart-shaped outer contour.
options.C: A septate uterus develops later in life from scar tissue, while a bicornuate uterus is always genetic.
options.D: A septate uterus is completely missing one fallopian tube, while a bicornuate uterus has both tubes.

explanation: Spot on! Think of it this way: a septate uterus looks normal on the outside but has a dividing wall inside, whereas a bicornuate uterus dips at the top, giving it a heart shape.

question: A patient agrees they are sick, stays home from classes, and asks family members if they look feverish. Which stage of illness is this?

options.A: Assumption of the sick role
options.B: Recovery and rehabilitation
options.C: Symptom experience
options.D: Dependent-patient role

explanation: When you step back from your daily duties and look for validation from loved ones that you need rest, you've entered the sick role.

question: What is a major hygiene worry for an infant in Gallows traction?

options.A: Urine and stool getting on the traction tapes and skin
options.B: Food clogging the metal pulleys
options.C: Saliva causing chest skin breakdown
options.D: Sweating causing quick dehydration

explanation: With the baby's hips up in the air and wearing a diaper in a tight spot, leaks happen. Keeping this area clean is a major nursing duty to stop infections!

question: How should the little prongs of a nasal cannula face when you put them into a patient's nose?

options.A: Flattened sideways
options.B: Pointing straight up
options.C: Curving downward
options.D: Tilted backward

explanation: They are shaped to match human anatomy! Pointing them downward ensures they slide comfortably along the natural curve of the nasal passages.

question: Which nutrient is especially critical for adolescent girls and boys during major growth spurts to support expanding blood volume?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Fiber
options.D: Iron

explanation: Iron is a core component of hemoglobin, which carries oxygen in the blood, making it vital during rapid adolescent growth. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h2)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care out in the community?

options.A: Health education, disease prevention, and personal empowerment
options.B: Performing major surgical operations in local community halls
options.C: Managing acute life-threatening trauma without medical backup
options.D: Enforcing strict hospital visiting hours and meal schedules

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses focus on teaching people how to stay healthy and take charge of their own wellness.

question: Why would an occupational health nurse schedule regular hearing (audiometric) tests for factory workers?

options.A: To evaluate stress from night shift rotations
options.B: To detect early signs of noise-induced hearing loss before it becomes permanent
options.C: To measure lung capacity after chemical dust exposure
options.D: To screen for bloodborne infections from shared gear

explanation: Spot on! Regular hearing tests help catch any hearing damage early on, before it turns into permanent deafness.

question: Why do doctors shorten the fertility testing timeline to just 6 months for women who are 35 or older?

options.A: Increased insurance coverage for fertility testing
options.B: Faster spread of sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Higher rates of voluntary childlessness in this group
options.D: Age-related decline in egg quality and reserve

explanation: Spot on! Because egg quality and number naturally start dropping faster after age 35, checking things a bit earlier helps protect their chances of starting a family.

question: What should a nurse do FIRST when an Alzheimer's patient suddenly becomes aggressive?

options.A: Immediately request a strong prescription sedative from the doctor
options.B: Look for unmet physical needs or triggers in the environment
options.C: Scold the patient firmly to stop the unacceptable behavior
options.D: Isolate the patient in a quiet, dark room until they fall asleep

explanation: You got it! Agitation is often how they express pain, hunger, or fear. Finding and fixing the trigger is always our best first nursing action!

question: What is the main difference between an acute care hospital and a long-term care (LTC) facility?

options.A: Hospitals focus solely on long-term chronic illnesses
options.B: LTC facilities serve as a long-term home focused on support
options.C: Hospitals provide more rehabilitation and personal care
options.D: LTC facilities only admit patients for short-term surgeries

explanation: You've got this! While hospitals are for short, emergency or curative visits, LTC facilities are designed to be a supportive home where residents live and receive ongoing care for extended periods.

question: What is a common result of supportive and transformational leadership on a hospital ward?

options.A: More communication breakdowns among health workers
options.B: Higher rates of preventable patient falls
options.C: Increased staff turnover and frequent nurse burnout
options.D: Lower medication errors and higher staff satisfaction

explanation: Supportive leadership builds a safe reporting culture and teamwork, which reduces errors and keeps nurses happy. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why is it so important to interview a patient alone when checking for gender-based violence?

options.A: To comply with laboratory protocols for collecting blood samples
options.B: To prevent the abuser from intimidating the patient or blocking disclosure
options.C: To allow the doctor to perform a physical examination faster
options.D: To speed up the hospital admission and bed allocation process

explanation: Spot on! Abusers often tag along to control the narrative. Speaking alone gives the patient a safe space to talk freely.

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) so important specifically in the TSSU decontamination zone?

options.A: Hospital management requires it only for decorative uniformity
options.B: It prevents dust from settling on the clean instruments
options.C: The temperature in that specific room is extremely high
options.D: Staff are exposed to blood splashes, contaminated water, and sharp tools

explanation: Spot on! Because you are washing blood-stained, used instruments, PPE acts as your shield against splashes, dirty water, and accidental needle pricks.

question: Which nursing action prevents skin damage (shear forces) when moving a patient up in bed?

options.A: Using a draw sheet to lift the patient slightly off the mattress
options.B: Applying heavy lotion to the patient's heels and sacrum
options.C: Pulling the patient quickly by their ankles across the sheets
options.D: Lowering the head of the bed completely flat before moving

explanation: Always lift, never drag! A draw sheet prevents friction that can tear delicate skin layers against the bed sheet.

question: Why does intravenous therapy carry a higher risk of severe adverse reactions compared to oral medications?

options.A: Patients are usually sicker when they receive IV drugs
options.B: Veins absorb medications much faster than stomach walls
options.C: Intravenous medications are always chemically stronger
options.D: The administered substance cannot be retrieved once injected

explanation: Direct entry into the circulation means an incorrect dose or allergic reaction takes effect immediately with no way to pump the stomach. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T4#GNS122_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why might you need to watch a patient for whole-body (systemic) effects after applying a topical cream or patch?

options.A: Skin application always causes widespread allergic reactions.
options.B: Topical drugs change the local skin temperature, affecting blood pressure.
options.C: Some topical agents are designed to cross the skin barrier and enter the bloodstream.
options.D: All topical drugs automatically travel to the liver first before working.

explanation: Spot on! While many stay local, formulations like transdermal patches are specially made to pass through the skin into the bloodstream to heal the whole body.

question: Why is oral care important right after a patient finishes a meal?

options.A: To remove leftover food particles and prevent bacterial growth
options.B: To stimulate the salivary glands to produce extra digestive acid
options.C: To cool down the patient's mouth temperature after warm food
options.D: To check if the patient's tooth enamel is strong enough
